title: Nested Repeat Decoding
statement:
Expand a compact string in which `k[text]` means `text` written `k` times.

Contract
- `encoded` is a non-null string, possibly empty, made only of lowercase letters `a`-`z`, digits, `[`, and `]`.
- It is always well formed. Digits appear only as a count `k` written immediately before a `[`; each count is between `1` and `300` with no leading zeros. Every `[` follows a count and has a matching `]`.
- `k[text]` decodes to the decoded `text` repeated `k` times. Groups may nest, may sit next to plain letters, and may be empty: `2[]` decodes to the empty string.
- Return the fully decoded string. Its length is at most `100,000`.

Examples
- `decode("3[a]2[bc]")` returns `"aaabcbc"`.
- `decode("2[x3[y]]z")` returns `"xyyyxyyyz"`: the inner group gives `yyy`, so each outer repetition is `xyyy`.
- `decode("10[k]")` returns `"kkkkkkkkkk"`, because counts can have more than one digit.
hints: Each `]` closes the most recently opened group, so inner groups always finish first. That last-opened, first-closed order is exactly what a stack models.

Keep the text built so far at the current level. When a count and `[` arrive, push the count and the current text and start a fresh level; when `]` arrives, pop them and append the finished level, repeated count times, to the restored text.

Counts can have several digits, so accumulate `count = count * 10 + digit` until the `[`. Build text with `StringBuilder` and `String.repeat` instead of repeated string concatenation. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(n) space for inputs with bounded nesting, where n is the length of the decoded string.
inputSyntax: Input: an encoded string of lowercase letters, counts, and brackets, for example: 2[x3[y]]z
